The mixing parameter is the share of each node's edges that leave its community, so the plain edges between communities grow from 2 to 5 to 9 and the communities get harder to tell apart." width="100%"} The Lancichinetti-Fortunato-Radicchi (LFR) benchmark is the standard test for community detection. Unlike the planted partition model, it gives the graph the heavy-tailed degrees and community sizes seen in real networks: - node degrees follow a power law with exponent `tau1`, with mean `average_degree` and maximum `max_degree` - community sizes follow a power law with exponent `tau2`, between `min_community` and `max_community` nodes - each node has a fraction `mu` of its edges (the mixing parameter) going to other communities and the rest inside its own The generator draws the degrees and community sizes, assigns nodes to communities (each community must be larger than the number of internal edges of each of its members), and then wires the internal and the external edges separately with the configuration model, swapping edge ends to remove self-loops, repeated edges, and "external" edges that land inside a community. The few edges that cannot be fixed this way are dropped, so the mean degree and the mixing come out slightly below their targets. The result is always a simple graph. Each node's community (`0`, `1`, ...) is stored in the `community_attr=` node attribute, and nodes are created community by community, so each community is a consecutive run of node IDs. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. LFR graphs are useful for: - benchmarking community detection methods, by sweeping `mu=` from clear (`0.1`) to hard (`0.5` and beyond) and comparing the result with the planted communities - generating realistic test networks with hubs and communities of many sizes - testing how measures behave on graphs with both community structure and heavy-tailed degrees ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes. Must be at least `2`. [mu]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Mixing parameter: the fraction of each node's edges that go to other communities, between `0` and `1`. Communities are clearly defined while `mu=` is below about `0.5`. [average_degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Target mean degree. Must lie between the smallest mean the power law allows (with a minimum degree of `1`) and `max_degree=`. [max_degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest allowed degree, at most `n - 1`. If `None` (default), it is `2.5` times `average_degree=` (capped at `n - 1`), the ratio used in the original benchmark studies. [tau1]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Exponent of the degree power law. Default is `2.0`; typical values are between `2` and `3`, and larger values give fewer hubs. [tau2]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1.0]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Exponent of the community size power law. Default is `1.0`; typical values are between `1` and `2`, and larger values give more small communities. [min_community]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Smallest community size. If `None` (default), it is the smallest degree in the power law. [max_community]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Largest community size. If `None` (default), it is `max_degree=` (or one more than the largest internal degree, if that is larger), capped at `n=`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [community_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["community"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's community. Default is `"community"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a parameter is out of range (`mu=` outside `0` to `1`, a negative or non-finite exponent, `n=` below `2`, `max_degree=` above `n - 1`, `average_degree=` out of reach of the degree distribution, or `min_community=` above `max_community=`), or if the communities cannot hold the nodes' internal degrees. In that case raising `max_community=`, lowering `max_degree=`, or raising `mu=` usually helps. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A 500-node benchmark with mean degree `10` and a mixing parameter of `0.2`: ::: {#ef0d3530 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_lfr_graph(n=500, mu=0.2, average_degree=10, seed=4) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges(), graph.get_node_df()["community"].n_unique() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (500, 2507, 43) ``` ::: ::: The degrees are heavy-tailed, from a minimum of a few edges up to `max_degree=` (here the default, `25`): ::: {#e064597f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} degrees = graph.get_node_df()["degree"] degrees.min(), round(degrees.mean(), 1), degrees.max() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 10.0, 25) ``` ::: ::: About `1 - mu = 0.8` of the edges fall inside a community, and Louvain finds a partition about as good as the planted one: ::: {#370fdacb .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} coverage, _ = graph.partition_quality("community") found = graph.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) planted, detected = graph.modularity("community"), graph.modularity(found) round(coverage, 2), round(planted, 2), round(detected, 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (0.8, 0.76, 0.77) ``` ::: ::: Raising `mu=` hides the communities: at `mu=0.6` most edges leave their community and the planted partition's modularity falls sharply: ::: {#af866ccc .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} mixed = ec.Graph().add_lfr_graph(n=500, mu=0.6, average_degree=10, seed=4) round(mixed.modularity("community"), 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` 0.37 ``` ::: :::
